rfi.title: EU tightens migration rules, eyes strategic enlargement in Balkans

Meanwhile, the question of EU enlargement is also on the cards at a Western Balkans summit.

rfi.description: The head of the World Health Organization  met with Félix Tshisekedi on Monday to discuss the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak, as an aid agency warned the epidemic was likely far larger than official figures suggest. The government said confirmed Ebola cases had risen to 321.

rfi.title: French health minister promises fast track access to mental health for youth
rfi.description: France's Health Minister Stéphanie Rist announced on Tuesday that the government would fast-track access to mental health appointments for young people. She promised that those identified by staff in the national education system as having mental health problems would be seen by a professional within 24 to 48 hours.

rfi.description: The head of The New York Times newspaper launched a scathing attack on artificial intelligence companies, accusing them of "shameless theft of intellectual property" and of threatening journalism. He was speaking at a global media congress on Monday in the southern French city of Marseille.

rfi.title: Cattelan’s famous taped banana stolen from French museum

rfi.title: Africa's finest: Morocco, African champions by ruling

rfi.title: Gulf states arrested over 1,000 for Iran war social media posts: Amnesty

rfi.title: Court rejects Rwanda €115mn claim against Britain over migrant deal
rfi.description: An international court on Monday rejected a claim by Rwanda for Britain to pay more than £100 million (€115million) it said London still owed from a scrapped deal to deport migrants.

rfi.title: Guineans denounce an 'electoral farce' after low turnout in legislative polls
rfi.description: Legislative and municipal elections were held in Guinea on Sunday to complete the process of returning constitutional order to the country after the December 2025 presidential election While this double ballot took place without major incident, voter turnout was low.

rfi.description: The French Navy has boarded another oil tanker from Russia as Paris steps up its campaign against Moscow’s so-called "shadow fleet" of vessels suspected of evading international sanctions.

rfi.title: Ethiopia election overshadowed by war, instability and muted opposition
rfi.description: Ethiopia goes to the polls on Monday in an election which is expected to return Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s Prosperity Party to power, but has been marked by instability, restricted voting and questions over whether the vote can challenge the status quo.

lemonde.description: La commune des Hauts-de-Seine est la ville française qui compte la plus forte proportion de ménages à très hauts revenus, selon une étude de l’Observatoire des inégalités, publiée mardi 2 juin. Le classement est dominé par l’Ouest parisien et les abords de Genève.

lemonde.description: L’ordre d’évacuation concerne sept localités du district de Bohodoukhiv, dans le nord-est de l’Ukraine, et quelque 7 000 personnes, dont plus de 1 700 enfants et 300 personnes à mobilité réduite.

lemonde.title: Les fruits et légumes bio associés à une baisse du risque de cancer du sein post-ménopause
lemonde.description: Selon des travaux français, pour chaque portion de 100 grammes de fruits et légumes conventionnels remplacés quotidiennement par leurs équivalents issus de l’agriculture biologique, le risque de développer un cancer du sein post-ménopausique est réduit de 10 %.

lemonde.description: L’Allemand Alexander Zverev a battu l’Espagnol Rafael Jodar et rallie le dernier carré du tournoi. Ce mardi a commencé par les deux premiers quarts féminins, dont un très beau duel entre les Ukrainiennes Elina Svitolina et Marta Kostyuk. La session nocturne voit le Tchèque Jakub Mensik et le Brésilien Joao Fonseca s’opposer.

lemonde.title: Patrick Poivre d’Arvor visé par deux nouvelles plaintes pour agressions sexuelles

lemonde.title: Au Pérou, l’ombre de l’ex-dictateur Alberto Fujimori plane sur le second tour de l’élection présidentielle
lemonde.description: Alors que Keiko Fujimori, fille de l’ex-autocrate Alberto Fujimori (1990-2000) condamné pour crimes contre l’humanité, est en bonne position pour être élue dimanche 7 juin, les familles des victimes de la violence d’Etat craignent le retour d’un régime autoritaire et se mobilisent pour faire acte de mémoire.

lemonde.description: Un responsable du Hezbollah a aussi menacé de riposte en cas d’attaque sur Beyrouth, dans une déclaration à l’Agence France-Presse. « L’ennemi sioniste doit savoir que toute agression contre la banlieue peut entraîner une réponse plus forte » de la part du Hezbollah, a-t-il écrit.

lemonde.title: Ruptures conventionnelles : le projet de loi réduisant la durée d’indemnisation définitivement adopté
lemonde.description: L’accord conclu entre les organisations patronales et les organisations syndicales prévoit notamment de ramener de 18 à 15 mois la durée maximale d’indemnisation pour les allocataires âgés de moins de 55 ans, après une fin de contrat de travail à l’amiable.

lemonde.description: A quelques jours de la date butoir des déclarations de revenus, le Collectif français du handicap visuel a assigné mardi la direction générale des finances publiques devant le tribunal administratif.

lemonde.description: Devant l’Assemblée nationale, le premier ministre a défendu les forces de l’ordre et plaidé pour que les auteurs de dégradations soient contraints à des « réparations ».

lemonde.title: Loi « Bétharram » : pourquoi l’Eglise de France s’opposait à la levée du secret de la confession
lemonde.description: L’article 9 de la proposition de loi, prévoyant d’obliger les prêtres à dénoncer les crimes sexuels contre les mineurs dont ils auraient pris connaissance, a finalement été supprimé par les députés en quête d’un compromis pour faire voter le texte.

lemonde.title: En Guinée, mort de Souleymane Diallo, directeur du dernier rempart de la presse libre
lemonde.description: Fondateur de l’hebdomadaire satyrique « Le Lynx », le journaliste est décédé lundi 1ᵉʳ juin. L’avenir du journal est aujourd’hui incertain, dans un environnement politique marqué par un durcissement du régime de Mamadi Doumbouya.

france24fr.description: Donald Trump a signé, mardi, un décret très attendu instituant un encadrement de l'IA aux États-Unis, au nom de la cybersécurité. Le texte entend notamment protéger les systèmes informatiques du pays face à des modèles d'IA désormais capables de repérer et d'exploiter des failles à une vitesse inédite.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle : ces images ne prouvent pas que le premier meeting de Gabriel Attal a été un “bide”
france24fr.description: Des internautes pro-russes affirment que le premier meeting pour la présidentielle 2027 de l’ancien Premier ministre français Gabriel Attal aurait été un échec : ils partagent comme preuves de prétendues photographies montrant un public clairsemé. Mais ces images ont été générées par intelligence artificielle.

france24fr.title: Union européenne : quatre questions sur les "hubs de retour" de migrants
france24fr.description: L’Union européenne devrait bientôt permettre à ses États membres de créer des "hubs de retour" dans des pays tiers, qui auront pour but d’accueillir les étrangers en situation irrégulière expulsés du territoire européen. Le texte est considéré comme une avancée en matière de politique migratoire par la droite et l’extrême droite, et comme un recul pour les droits humains par la gauche. Explications.

france24fr.title: ⚽Mondial 2026 : Macron rend visite aux Bleus à Clairefontaine
france24fr.description: 🇫🇷 À quelques jours du début de la Coupe du monde, le président Emmanuel #Macron s'est rendu à #Clairefontaine pour soutenir l'équipe de #France, qui s'envolera bientôt pour New York afin d'y disputer son premier match contre le Sénégal le 16 juin.⚽

france24fr.title: Quand la Chine rêve d’identifier les futurs opposants politiques grâce à l’IA
france24fr.description: L’entreprise chinoise Geedge Network, déjà accusée d’avoir vendu le système de censure numérique chinois à d’autres pays, planche également sur la possibilité de laisser l’IA déceler qui pourrait à l'avenir devenir un opposant politique. Un rêve pour tout régime autoritaire et un cauchemar pour les défenseurs des droits humains ?

france24fr.title: L'ONU alerte sur un probable épisode du phénomène El Niño "modéré voir fort" cet été
france24fr.description: Le développement d'un épisode El Niño est probable à 80% entre juin et août, augmentant le risque d'événements météorologiques extrêmes dans les prochains mois, a alerté mardi l'Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM).

france24fr.title: Malgré les promesses de désescalade, Israël mène des attaques meurtrières au Sud-Liban
france24fr.description: Israël a poursuivi ses frappes sur le Sud-Liban mardi, faisant plusieurs morts dont des enfants, au lendemain de la demande du président américain, Donald Trump, au Premier ministre israélien, Benjamin Netanyahu, de ne pas attaquer Beyrouth afin d'éviter une nouvelle escalade.

france24fr.title: Avec le Salon Computex, Taiwan est le berceau de la révolution IA
france24fr.description: Le président taiwanais a inauguré le salon “Computex” basé sur les nouvelles technologies.  L'événement se décrit comme la plus grande exposition sur l'IA jamais réalisée et se déroule sur l'île devenue au fil des années une super star de l'intelligence artificielle. Un atout sur lequel se base le gouvernement taiwanais pour assurer sa sauvegarde politique à l'échelle internationale.

france24fr.title: Rwanda-France : un mémorial pour les victimes du génocide inaugurée à Paris
france24fr.description: Ce mardi 2 juin, le chef de l'État rwandais, Paul Kagame, se rend dans la capitale française pour inaugurer en compagnie d'Emmanuel Macron une double stèle en mémoire des victimes du génocide des Tutsis au Rwanda. Un nouveau geste mémoriel de Paris pour sceller la réconciliation entre les deux pays.

france24fr.title: Les pourparlers reprennent : quatrième cycle de négociations entre Israël et le Liban
france24fr.description: Les ambassadeurs d'Israël et du Liban ont été reçus mardi au département d'Etat pour une nouvelle session de pourparlers directs, alors qu'Israël et le Hezbollah ont échangé des tirs après que Donald Trump a affirmé avoir reçu l'engagement d'un apaisement de la part des deux camps. Les précisions avec notre correspondant à Washington, Matthieu Mabin.

france24fr.title: Léon XIV nomme une femme laïque à la tête d'un "ministère", une première historique
france24fr.description: Le pape Léon XIV a nommé, mardi, pour la première fois dans l'histoire du Vatican une femme laïque à un dicastère. La Mexicano-Américaine María Montserrat Alvarado deviendra en novembre "préfète du dicastère pour la Communication". Cette nomination se range dans les efforts de réforme du Vatican portée par le souverain pontife.

france24fr.title: Derrière l'image : Thomas Pesquet, départ vers l'espace en 2027 pour une mission privée
france24fr.description: Les deux astronautes Thomas Pesquet et Arnaud Prost partiront dans l'espace en 2027 dans le cadre d'un accord signé entre la France et l'entreprise spatiale américaine Vast, a annoncé lundi Emmanuel Macron.

france24fr.title: Roland-Garros 2026 : Svitolina éliminée, Andreeva en maîtrise
france24fr.description: Les quarts de finale de Roland-Garros débutent ce mardi. En attendant les résultats du tableau masculin, ceux du tableau féminin réservent une assez grosse surprise. L'Ukrainienne Elina Svitolina, tête de série n°7, s'arrête à ce stade de la compétition, tandis que Mirra Andreeva s'est tranquillement imposée sur le court central.

france24fr.title: Liban : Israël appelle à évacuer Nabatieh
france24fr.description: Des frappes israéliennes lundi sur la ville de Tyr, dans le sud du Liban, ont tué quatre personnes et blessé 127 autres, dont 39 membres du personnel d'un hôpital, a annoncé mardi le ministère libanais de la Santé.

france24fr.title: Attaque russe d'ampleur en Ukraine : au moins 18 morts dans le pays
france24fr.description: Une attaque russe contre l'Ukraine tôt mardi a fait au moins 18 morts, dont six dans la capitale touchée par des missiles balistiques, a indiqué Kiev en réitérant son appel urgent à une aide américaine pour des systèmes de défense antiaérienne.

france24fr.title: En Guinée, les électeurs sont dans l'attente des résultats
france24fr.description: En Guinée, au lendemain du double scrutin législatif et communal, les opérations de dépouillement des bulletins et de centralisation des procès-verbaux se poursuivent à travers le pays. Dans une interview accordée à France 24, la directrice générale des élections a promis des élections libres, crédibles et transparentes. Les résultats officiels seraient disponibles dans un délai de 48 h.

france24fr.title: Décryptage : progression importante d'Israël dans le sud Liban
france24fr.description: Les ambassadeurs d'Israël et du Liban ont été reçus mardi au département d'Etat pour une nouvelle session de pourparlers directs, alors qu'Israël et le Hezbollah ont échangé des tirs après que Donald Trump a affirmé avoir reçu l'engagement d'un apaisement de la part des deux camps. france24fr.title: L'UE durcit sa politique migratoire : installation des centres en dehors de l'Europe
france24fr.description: Les eurodéputés et les Etats européens ont trouvé un accord lundi soir pour durcir la politique migratoire de l'UE, avec la possibilité de créer des centres à l'étranger où renvoyer les migrants illégaux. Certains pays européens comme le Danemark, l'Autriche ou l'Allemagne commencent déjà à imaginer où installer ces centres, par exemple au Rwanda, en Ouganda ou en Ouzbékistan.

spiegel.description: Deutschland bekommt zwei Außenstellen von Yad Vashem. Nach der Entscheidung warnen Kritiker vor israelischer Einflussnahme. Dabei zeigt ausgerechnet der Protest, wie groß die Leerstellen im deutschen Holocaustgedenken sind.

spiegel.title: Uno-Generalversammlung: Khalilur Rahman übernimmt von Annalena Baerbock »einen der besten Jobs der Welt«
spiegel.description: Ab September wird Khalilur Rahman neuer Präsident der Uno-Vollversammlung und folgt auf Annalena Baerbock. Der früheren Außenministerin attestieren Experten in ihrer Amtszeit eine »zupackende Führungspersönlichkeit«.

spiegel.title: FDP: Wolfgang Kubicki und Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann - Ausgleich nach Machtkampf
spiegel.description: Nach dem Duell um den Vorsitz flogen verbale Spitzen, nun senden der neue FDP-Chef Kubicki und die unterlegene Strack-Zimmermann versöhnliche Töne. Kann der Frieden halten?

spiegel.title: Donald Trump soll Benjamin Netanyahu wüst beschimpft haben
spiegel.description: Weil Israel im Libanon weiter angreifen will, soll US-Präsident Trump seinen Verbündeten scharf angegangen sein: »You’re fucking crazy« soll er zu Netanyahu gesagt haben. Währenddessen gehen die Kampfhandlungen offenbar weiter.

spiegel.title: Achim Lippoth: Kinderfotograf wegen sexuellem Missbrauchs zu sieben Jahren Haft verurteilt
spiegel.description: Ein erstes Urteil hatte der BGH wegen Verfahrensfehlern zurückverwiesen, nun muss Achim Lippoth deutlich länger ins Gefängnis.

spiegel.title: Alkohol am Steuer: Auch im Parkhaus ist eine Fahrt mit Alkohol im Blut strafbar
spiegel.description: Er wollte mit knapp zwei Promille aus einem Nürnberger Parkhaus herausfahren, doch eine Mitarbeiterin sperrte die Schranke. Der Mann hielt sein Handeln nicht für strafbar, mehrere Gerichtsinstanzen schon.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: So wollen die Europäer Wladimir Putin an den Verhandlungstisch bringen
spiegel.description: Noch scheint der russische Machthaber nicht zu ernsthaften Verhandlungen über ein Ende des Angriffskriegs gegen die Ukraine bereit. Die Bundesregierung glaubt aber, das könne sich ändern. Entscheidend seien dafür zwei Dinge.

spiegel.title: »dariadaria« über Armedangels: Warum sie die Kooperation pausiert – und selbst mit fairer Mode hadert
spiegel.description: Der SPIEGEL hat über Missstände beim Modelabel Armedangels berichtet. Hier erklärt Influencerin Madeleine Darya Alizadeh, bekannt als »dariadaria«, warum sie die Kooperation pausiert – und selbst mit fairer Mode hadert.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Was die Handys osteuropäischer Frachtgutdiebe über den Louvre-Raub verraten
spiegel.description: In Belgien sind Ermittler auf verdächtige Handyfotos aus dem Louvre gestoßen. Die neue Fährte nährt Befürchtungen: Frankreichs Kronjuwelen könnten längst auf dem Schwarzmarkt von Antwerpen verscherbelt worden sein.

spiegel.title: Ungarn: Péter Magyar verliert bei Antrittsbesuch im Kanzleramt die Fassung
spiegel.description: Kanzler Merz setzt große Hoffnungen auf Ungarns neuen Regierungschef Péter Magyar. Der Antrittsbesuch verläuft harmonisch – bis Magyar zu einem Machtkampf im eigenen Land gefragt wird.

spiegel.title: Markus Söder und Carsten Linnemann fahren bei der Seeheimer Spargelfahrt der SPD mit
spiegel.description: In der Koalition läuft es nicht gut. Jetzt kommen CSU-Chef Söder und CDU-Generalsekretär Linnemann zur jährlichen Spargelfahrt konservativer Sozialdemokraten. Kann das helfen?

spiegel.title: Stanley Cup und Pokémon: Die Sammelleidenschaft der Vegas Golden Knights
spiegel.description: Das Eishockeyteam Vegas Golden Knights steht im Finale des Stanley Cups. Sollte ihnen der Gewinn der Meisterschaft gelingen, hat das eventuell auch ein bisschen mit Pikachu, Schiggy und Glurak zu tun.

spiegel.title: Rhabarber: Alles über das süß-saure Gemüse
spiegel.description: Wissen Sie, was die Erfindung von Limette-Ingwer-Limo mit einer Rhabarbermissernte zu tun hat? Und wie man den zartesten Rhabarber der Welt macht? Nein? Dann kommt dieser Text wie gerufen.

spiegel.title: Haftbefehls Frau Nina Anhan veröffentlicht Ballermann-Schlager »Nackige Frau«
spiegel.description: Ihr Mann rappte gerade auf dem Ballermann, jetzt will auch Haftbefehls Ehefrau Nina Anhan nachziehen. Zusammen mit dem »Layla«-Produzenten hat sie ein Video für ihren Partyschlager »Nackige Frau« gedreht – auf Mallorca.

spiegel.title: Norwegen: Schiffswrack aus dem 18. Jahrhundert entdeckt
spiegel.description: Als hätten sie eine Zeitkapsel gefunden: Vor Norwegens Küste haben Forscher ein Schiffswrack aus dem 18. Jahrhundert entdeckt, voll mit chinesischem Porzellan. Sie hoffen auf weitere Schätze.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Streit der Assauer-Erben, Iran-Krieg, Eintritt für den Kölner Dom
spiegel.description: Der Kölner Dom kostet ab Juli Eintritt. Iran droht mit dem Abbruch der Verhandlungen mit den USA. Und Rudi Assauers Tochter und seine Ex-Sekretärin sind angeklagt. Das ist die Lage am Dienstagabend.

spiegel.title: Russlands Krieg gegen Ukraine: Auf der Krim wird das Benzin knapp, Ukraine meldet weitere Tote
spiegel.description: Weil die Ukraine russische Versorgungswege attackiert, kommt es auf der Krim zu Treibstoffengpässen. Und: In Dnipro und Kyjiw sind die Opferzahlen nach russischen Attacken gestiegen.

spiegel.title: French Open: Alexander Zverev besiegt Rafael Jodar und steht im Halbfinale
spiegel.description: Alexander Zverev benötigt nur noch zwei Siege bis zum ersten Triumph bei einem Grand-Slam-Turnier. Jungstar Rafael Jódar war im Viertelfinale der French Open chancenlos gegen den Deutschen.

observador.title: Adega de Estaline com 20 mil garrafas vai a leilão
observador.description: Ditador soviético foi o guardião da coleção confiscada pelos comunistas aos czares russos. Colecionadores que viajaram de todo o mundo estão preocupados com a conservação das garrafas.

observador.title: Heranças. Governo elogia oposição e admite "ajustes" na lei
observador.description: Proposta do Governo para a reformulação das heranças indivisas é votada nesta quarta-feira na generalidade. Governo lança aviso para o debate na especialidade: "Não reformar não é opção".

observador.title: Pena suspensa por anomalia psíquica. Justiça para Salgado?
observador.description: O jornalista João Paulo Godinho e o presidente da Associação Sindical dos Juízes Portugueses, Nuno Matos, explicam os critérios e o impacto da doença de Alzheimer na decisão do tribunal.

observador.title: Águas de Gaia. Preventiva para empreiteiro e ex-diretor
observador.description: Preventiva para José António Martins e o empresário António Santos Mota. Dois funcionários ficam com pulseira eletrónica e atual diretora da empresa foi suspensa de funções e proibida de contactos.

observador.title: 18h. PM: Maioria dos portugueses vai trabalhar amanhã
observador.description: Luís Montenegro apela para que a paralisação não prejudique quem quer trabalhar. Ainda, Os chapéus-de-sol podem ser colocados à frente das zonas concessionadas das praias portuguesas.

observador.title: Paula Cardoso, do PSD: "Não vejo como afastar o Chega do TC"
observador.description: A presidente da comissão de Assuntos Constitucionais e deputada do PSD defende que o Chega "tem direito a indicar" nomes para o TC por causa da representatividade que conquistou e ataca Passos Coelho.

observador.title: CAP afasta-se do Plano de Restauro da Natureza do Governo
observador.description: A Confederação dos Agricultores de Portugal acusou o Governo de avançar com o Plano sem discutir previamente as medidas e instou a reunião extraordinária de comissão de acompanhamento.

observador.title: Miguel Albuquerque pondera não presidir ao congresso do PSD
observador.description: Presidente do governo regional atacou Montenegro e garantiu que, com o atual "diálogo de surdos" com o Executivo, não irá presidir ao congresso do PSD, a 20 e 21 de junho.

observador.title: PSP acompanhou cimeira de extrema-direita na Figueira da Foz
observador.description: Remigration Summit foi organizada por Afonso Gonçalves, líder do movimento político Reconquista que está a ser investigado por discurso de ódio.

observador.title: Que serviços mínimos vão ter os transportes e a aviação
observador.description: Com a exceção do Metro de Lisboa e da Transtejo, os principais operadores de transportes públicos vão ter serviços mínimos no dia da greve geral. TAP, Easyjet, Raynair e SATA também cumprem mínimos.

observador.title: Diretor clínico da ULS Lisboa Ocidental demite-se
observador.description: João Gamela demite-se do cargo numa altura em que existem várias denúncias sobre o ambiente de trabalho vivido. O especialista, de 65 anos, justificou a saída por razões pessoais.

observador.title: IRN com serviços mínimos no dia da greve geral
observador.description: Os serviços digitais a que é possível aceder online no portal do IRN, sem necessidade de deslocações aos balcões físicos, permanecem disponíveis sem constrangimentos no dia da greve.

observador.title: Bruno Batista: "Marco Silva dá um sinal ao sair do Fulham"
observador.description: Técnico português está cada vez mais perto da Luz. Ex-candidato à vice-presidência do clube vê notícia como positiva e acredita que Marco Silva privilegiou o projeto encarnado ao dinheiro.

observador.title: Navios dos "Piratas das Caraíbas" encontrados em Nassau
observador.description: Canhões, balas, cachimbos e um casco carbonizado: arqueólogos encontraram os primeiros vestígios subaquáticos da "República dos Piratas" que reinou na Ilha de Nova Providência entre 1713 e 1718.

observador.title: Bicicletas e trotinetes. Associação quer clarificar normas
observador.description: A Associação Nacional das Indústrias de Duas Rodas lamenta assistir à comercialização, adulteração e circulação de veículos que não cumprem minimamente os requisitos técnicos e legais exigidos.

observador.title: Greve dos enfermeiros na ULS da Arrábida com adesão de 70%
observador.description: Os números da adesão à greve demonstram o descontentamento dos enfermeiros, referiu o sindicato, destacando sobretudo a discriminação sentida no pagamento dos retroativos das progressões de carreira.

observador.title: 17h. Futebol. Treinador Marco Silva está de saída do Fulham
observador.description: O anúncio surge depois da imprensa desportiva dizer Marco Silva pode ter acordo fechado com o Benfica. Ainda, o primeiro-ministro pede que a greve geral não afete os portugueses que querem trabalhar.

observador.title: Direita aconselha PS a largar "síndrome de Fernanda Câncio"
observador.description: Ventura e Rui Rocha acusaram PS de não aprender com lições do passado e de continuar a funcionar como "um polvo de corrupção". Na resposta, Brilhante Dias disse que partido não tem "medo" da direita.

elpais.title: Feijóo, sobre ir a Waterloo a negociar con Puigdemont la moción de censura: “Hablemos de cosas serias”
elpais.description: “Devolveré la decencia a mi país con ayuda o sin ella”, asegura el líder del PP en su intervención en el Círculo de Economía

elpais.title: El PSOE eleva ahora de 15.000 a casi 45.000 euros el importe que pagó a Leire Díez por labores de comunicación
elpais.description: El partido detalla los pagos a la exmilitante por su trabajo en Cantabria hace casi una década en un escrito al juzgado de Madrid que investiga una causa distinta a la que llevó a la Audiencia Nacional a enviar a la UCO a Ferraz

elpais.title: La defensa de David Sánchez, a una testigo clave de las acusaciones: “¿Por qué no interpuso denuncia en 2017?”
elpais.description: Cristina de Frutos, que aspiraba al puesto que finalmente logró el hermano del presidente, insiste en sus sospechas sobre la adjudicación sin aportar pruebas

elpais.title: La princesa Leonor, primera paracaidista de la Familia Real
elpais.description: Zarzuela difunde imágenes de la heredera preparándose para saltar en Alcantarilla (Murcia) como parte de su formación militar

elpais.title: Jódar sucumbe a la majestuosidad de Zverev en Roland Garros
elpais.description: El alemán ofrece un recital, tras un primer set muy debatido, y accede por quinta vez a las semifinales en las seis últimas ediciones: 7-6(3), 6-1 y 6-3, tras 2h 25m

elpais.title: “Han ido a pillar”: casi toda España se suma a la PAU en una Selectividad blindada con detectores de frecuencia
elpais.description: La adolescencia, Manuel Vicent, Emilia Pardo Bazán y la invasión musulmana de la Península, en las preguntas de los ejercicios

elpais.title: Presunta imparcialidad
elpais.description: El doble rasero judicial y policial acaba erosionando la legitimidad de un poder fundamental del Estado

elpais.title: Las reinas no fuman
elpais.description: El mensaje general de doña Letizia casi parecía dirigido a alguien en particular

elpais.title: Bruselas cede y se abre a relajar las reglas de gasto público para que los Estados afronten la crisis energética
elpais.description: La Comisión plantea que los Gobiernos puedan destinar hasta un 0,3% del PIB anual para reducir la dependencia de los combustibles fósiles

elpais.title: Petro insiste en cuestionar las elecciones: “Presento las bases comprobadas del posible fraude”
elpais.description: El presidente colombiano señala un aumento de mesas y cédulas en uno de los varios ‘softwares’ electorales

elpais.title: Putin anuncia una “nueva dimensión” en la guerra contra Ucrania y lanza un intenso ataque que mata al menos a 22 personas
elpais.description: La ofensiva del Kremlin, una de las peores de los últimos meses, golpea Kiev, Dnipró y Járkov y causa un centenar de heridos

elpais.title: Israel y Hezbolá mantienen el fuego cruzado pese al anuncio de Trump del fin de las hostilidades en Líbano
elpais.description: Netanyahu sale escaldado de su plan de bombardear Beirut. Según el medio digital Axios, el presidente de Estados Unidos abroncó por teléfono al líder israelí: “Eres un puto loco”

elpais.title: Marco Rubio sobre la crisis con Cuba: “Hemos hablado con ellos y les hemos dicho lo que tienen que hacer para recuperar su economía”
elpais.description: El secretario de Estado acusa a las autoridades cubanas de patrocinar el terrorismo y de trabajar para el espionaje chino y ruso

elpais.title: Iberostar deja doce hoteles en Cuba por la amenaza de sanciones de Estados Unidos y eleva la presión sobre Meliá
elpais.description: La hotelera balear confirma que abandona la gestión de esos establecimientos, propiedad de Gaesa, el conglomerado militar en el punto de mira de la Administración Trump

elpais.title: Anticorrupción apunta a “nuevas imputaciones” por los presuntos amaños de obra pública del ‘caso Koldo’
elpais.description: El fiscal pide a la Audiencia Nacional que prorrogue otros seis meses la investigación sobre esta presunta trama

elpais.title: El Papa nombra jefa de comunicación del Vaticano a la presidenta de una televisión ultraconservadora de EE UU, hostil a Francisco
elpais.description: María Montserrat Alvarado, de origen mexicano, es la primera mujer laica en un cargo tan alto en la Santa Sede. El pontífice argentino llegó a definir como “obra del diablo” los ataques de la cadena EWTN

elpais.title: La inminente llegada de ‘El Niño’ echará “más leña al fuego de un mundo que se calienta”
elpais.description: La Organización Meteorológica Mundial insta a estar preparados ante el riesgo de aumento de los fenómenos extremos alimentados por este evento natural

elpais.title: Illa y Rueda chocan en público por la financiación autonómica: “No hay que jugar a las bilateralidades”
elpais.description: El ‘president’ advierte en el Cercle d’Economia que un Gobierno que dependa de Vox implicará una involución territorial

nyt.title: Iran War Live Updates: Israel Strikes Southern Lebanon After Pulling Back From Threat to Beirut
nyt.description: Under pressure from President Trump, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel held off from attacking Beirut. But he vowed to continue Israel’s campaign against Hezbollah, which could threaten peace negotiations with Iran.

nyt.title: Housing Official Who Attacked Democrats Invokes a Disputed Family Legacy
nyt.description: The Trump nominee Bill Pulte has called out a Fed governor and New York’s attorney general for issues with their mortgage documents. Some leaders of the family’s home-building business bristle at how he has enhanced his reputation.

nyt.title: New Proposal Would Allow Administration to Block Grants if They Don’t Support Trump’s Agenda
nyt.description: A new proposal would allow the administration to block grants if they do not satisfy President Trump’s agenda or support what it calls “anti-American” values.

nyt.title: Trump Signs Executive Order Seeking Oversight of A.I. Models
nyt.description: The order, which signaled a shift from the hands-off approach the White House had previously taken toward A.I., followed debates over how to gain control of A.I. models without disrupting innovation.

nyt.title: What to Watch in Tuesday’s Primary Elections in Iowa, Montana and Beyond
nyt.description: Democrats have a competitive Senate primary race in Iowa, where the party is hoping to make gains, while a smokejumper is running in a contested House primary in Montana.

nyt.title: Trump Endorses Tom Kean Jr., the N.J. Congressman Who Hasn’t Been Seen For Months
nyt.description: The message from President Trump about Representative Thomas Kean Jr. comes as voters head to the polls on Tuesday. Mr. Kean’s name is on the ballot, but he hasn’t been seen for months.

nyt.title: A Congressman Was Suddenly Absent. So We Looked. And Looked.
nyt.description: Will the mystery of Tom Kean Jr., a New Jersey representative, finally be solved on Tuesday? The reporters covering the story will have questions.

nyt.title: How Three Chess Friends Battled Demons and Saved Two Lives
nyt.description: A homeless chess hustler, a scholar and an aging recluse found hope in a trashed apartment by Central Park.

nyt.title: Only the Right Tests Can Stop This Ebola Outbreak. Congo Has Hardly Any.
nyt.description: A chronic lack of investment in development of better tests has left clinicians blind and allows deadly viruses to spread unchecked.

nyt.title: U.S. Ebola Unit Plans in Kenya, Subject of Protests, Suffers New Setback From Court Ruling
nyt.description: The court further delayed the Trump administration’s proposed quarantine unit for Americans exposed to the virus. The plan has sparked angry protests in Kenya.

nyt.title: Obama Center’s Two Sides: A Lovely Park and a Forbidding Tower
nyt.description: In Chicago, the $850 million Obama Presidential Center aims to remake a neighborhood with a 19.3-acre community hub and a brooding 225-foot museum.

nyt.title: Russia Launches Deadly Strikes on Kyiv After Threatening Ukraine for a Week
nyt.description: Moscow’s repeated warnings of a major strike, combined with the delay before it happened, seemed intended to inflict a psychological toll on the Ukrainian capital.

nyt.title: Bombs Raining Down on Ukraine Can’t Hide Signs of Russia’s Faltering War
nyt.description: The war has not been going the Kremlin’s way, with battleground losses and growing casualties. With fiercer strikes, Moscow hopes to gain a better position for negotiations.

nyt.title: What Ireland and Germany Can Teach Us About Birthright Citizenship
nyt.description: President Trump has argued that the United States is “stupid” for granting citizenship at birth. Most countries don’t do so, but that can create problems.

nyt.title: ‘La La Land’ Orchestral Performance Saved by Keyboardist in the Audience
nyt.description: After a musician fell ill during a live performance of the score from “La La Land,” the composer Justin Hurwitz asked for a sight reader. A 21-year-old student stepped up.

nyt.title: Netanyahu’s Critics Accuse Him of Running Israel as a U.S. ‘Vassal State’
nyt.description: Critics pounced on the Israeli prime minister after President Trump claimed on social media he had persuaded him to call off “a major raid” on Hezbollah in Beirut.

nyt.title: Lebanon Endures Threats, Diplomacy and Whiplash as Others Decide Its Fate
nyt.description: The conflict between the United States, Israel and Iran looms over a state that has been pummeled by military strikes but has little say in determining its own future.

nyt.title: Iran Reveals 3-Day Funeral Plan for Ayatollah Khamenei, After Long Delay
nyt.description: Ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei will be held in multiple cities, including Tehran, where authorities expect up to 20 million people to attend, Iranian state media reported.

republika.title: Guerra Ucraina-Russia, news. Kiev annuncia l’evacuazione di villaggi nella regione di Kharkiv
republika.description: Media: “Almeno 21 morti nei raid russi”. Palazzi in fiamme a Kiev. Ft: “Gli Usa stanno discutendo l’idea di armi nucleari in altri Paesi Nato”

republika.title: Mattarella ai giovani: “Preoccupano gli uomini soli al comando, l’immigrazione non è un problema”
republika.description: Il capo dello Stato risponde al Quirinale in occasione del 2 giugno

republika.title: Guerra in Iran, le news. Rubio: “Trattiamo, accordo possibile oggi, domani o la prossima settimana”
republika.description: Tajani: “La pace? Sono gli Usa che devono fermare Israele”. Raid di Israele in Libano: almeno otto morti, tre sono bambini. Bozza del summit Ue: “Lavorare sulle sanzioni ai ministri estremisti di Israele”. Nave Msc colpita dai pasdaran in un porto iracheno

republika.title: Strage dei braccianti, il monito della Cei: “Basta con il silenzio sporco delle convenienze"
republika.description: Vannacci invoca la remigrazione, il governo chiede si faccia piena luce sul dramma di Amendolara. Il Pd: “ Ecco cosa significa essere un invisibile nelle campagne del Sud”

republika.title: Zerocalcare e le polemiche su “Due spicci”: “Problemi? Potevano contattarmi, io sono un alleato”
republika.description: L’artista replica, con un video, alle accuse sulle condizioni di lavoro degli animatori coinvolti nella sua nuova serie animata e attacca Gasparri: “Fa il giustiziere e poi vota contro il salario minimo”

republika.title: Zverev, continua la caccia al primo Slam: battuto Jodar, è in semifinale al Roland Garros
republika.description: Il tedesco, grande favorito dopo l’uscita di Sinner, mette fine alla corsa del giovane spagnolo. Bolelli e Vavassori avanti nel doppio

republika.title: Nuova gaffe di Tajani: “Conte e Schlein assenti al 2 giugno”. Ma il cerimoniale non prevede i leader
republika.description: Il vicepremier, parlando del forfait di Salvini, ha commentato che mancavano anche il presidente del Movimento 5 stelle e la leader del Pd

republika.title: Alcaraz torna ad allenarsi, ma solo con la mano sinistra: come procede il recupero dall’infortunio
republika.description: Lo spagnolo, fermo da aprile per un problema al polso destro, ha pubblicato un video in cui si allena impugnando la racchetta con la mano sinistra, mentre l’altro braccio si limita a simulare i movimenti

republika.title: Fuga dei cavalli sulla Colombo, si indaga sull’agente che ha acceso i fuochi
republika.description: Ipotizzati i reati di accensioni e esplosioni pericolose aggravate dall'abuso della funzione pubblica e lesioni. Gli investigatori verificano anche il ruolo di altri agenti presenti alle Terme di Caracalla.

republika.title: Amendolara, c’è un bracciante sopravvissuto: “Ci davano casa e da mangiare ma non i soldi”
republika.description: Il racconto del cittadino afghano rimasto ferito: “Hanno buttato la benzina e poi hanno dato fuoco all’auto. Io sono fuggito dal portellone lasciato aperto”

republika.title: Bad Bunny, la “casita” vip del tour mondiale finisce in tribunale
republika.description: Tanti gli ospiti sul palco che l’hanno visitata: da Chiara Ferragni ad Ana de Armas. Il simbolo dei concerti dell’artista, però, finisce al centro di una causa milionaria

republika.title: Propaganda Isis, resta in carcere il ventunenne fermato in Brianza. La gip: “Pericoloso socialmente”
republika.description: Convalidato il fermo di Zakaria Ben Haddi. Le sue parole: “Sì, quegli account sono miei ma non volevo fare apologia”

republika.title: Parata 2 giugno, fermati sei ambientalisti: preparavano un blitz all’Altare della Patria
republika.description: Gli attivisti di Extinction Rebellion fermati dalla polizia vicino al cantiere della metro con uno striscione di grandi dimensioni e fumogeni. Denunciati per invasione di terreni ed edifici, tre anche per resistenza

republika.title: L'ultima sfilata, poi il meritato riposo: oggi va in pensione Briciola, la mascotte dei carabinieri
republika.description: La cagnolina partecipa alla parata del 2 giugno per l’ultima volta. Divenne famosa nel 2015, con la capriola davanti a Mattarella

republika.title: Migranti, accordo Ue sui rimpatri: ok ai return hub in Paesi terzi e al foglio di via europeo
republika.description: Tra dieci giorni entrerà in vigore il nuovo Patto asilo – diverso dal protocollo Italia-Albania – e il governo Meloni dovrà ricorrere a un nuovo decreto con le principali disposizioni contenute nel ddl immigrazione ancora fermo in Senato e l’adeguamento alle norme europee, più la reintroduzione del blocco navale

republika.title: Unicredit vola al 50% in Commerzbank grazie a maggiori adesioni all’Ops e nuovi derivati
republika.description: I titoli consegnati all’offerta salgono al 7,58%, da sommare al 26,8% in azioni detenute e ai derivati, saliti al 13,1% potenziale. La banca: “Già raggiunto il primo obiettivo del 30%, che dà certezza e flessibilità per ulteriori acquisti futuri”

republika.title: Xenia Fedorova, il volto dei media Bolloré che fa infuriare Parigi: “Propagandista russa”

phys-org.description: Sometime between 5.5 and 5.6 million years ago, two shell crushers squared off in the languid currents of an ancient Florida river. The fossils they left behind, discovered by paleontologists at the Florida Museum of Natural History, reveal the identity of the combatants and the outcome of their encounter.

phys-org.description: Two French astronauts are to blast into space next year, one of whom will stay on board the world's first commercial space station, under a new deal sealed between France and the U.S. company Vast.

phys-org.title: A new origin story for multicellular life points to physics, not genes alone
phys-org.description: How did life make the leap from single cells to coordinated, multicellular organisms? And how do genetically identical cells still perform a version of that feat every time an embryo begins to take shape?

phys-org.title: How megalomaniac leaders establish their grip on a group—and how they lose it
phys-org.description: Megalomaniacal leaders are fascinating. They exude boundless confidence, harbor sometimes excessive ambitions and make decisions that are often out of touch with reality.

phys-org.title: First-of-its-kind AI tool for translating life-saving weather warnings across the US advanced
phys-org.description: Nearly 69 million people in the United States speak a language other than English at home, yet weather warnings have long been issued almost exclusively in English. A new study documents how the National Weather Service is using artificial intelligence to change that, developing a comprehensive translation program that delivers life-saving forecasts and alerts in Spanish, Chinese, Vietnamese, Samoan, French and other languages.

phys-org.title: Antibiotic resistance turns up in Australian horses, raising new concerns about animal and human infections
phys-org.description: Research into a common environmental germ that can cause severe infections in people and animals has raised concern that horses are starting to develop antibiotic resistance towards it. The University of the Sunshine Coast study examined the prevalence of the bug P. aeruginosa in Australian wild birds, native wildlife, livestock and domestic animals.

phys-org.title: Centuries‑old logbooks reveal how bowhead whales are recovering from near extinction
phys-org.description: Bowhead whales have the greatest life span of any mammal on Earth. They can reach over 200 years in age thanks in part to their slow metabolism and cancer-suppressing genes.

phys-org.title: Mathematicians say 'don't believe hype' on AI capabilities
phys-org.description: Dozens of mathematicians signed a declaration Tuesday calling for the discipline to resist beating the drum for artificial intelligence developers.

phys-org.title: Twilight hunt reveals falcon feasting on unusual prey at Greek lagoon
phys-org.description: Falcons are lauded for their speed and agility. The Eurasian Hobby (Falco subbuteo), skilled at snagging birds and insects out of the air, is no exception. However, during twilight on one day in October, researcher Apostolos Christopoulos observed several hobbies feeding on something else in a protected wetland in Greece—bats from the genus Pipistrellus.

phys-org.title: Distant climate patterns determine how cold Japan's winters become
phys-org.description: Researchers have uncovered a key mechanism behind Japan's extreme winter weather, revealing how distant climate patterns interact to intensify cold waves and heavy snowfall.

phys-org.title: Bird masturbation appears natural across 120 species, challenging long-held veterinary advice
phys-org.description: New research has found that masturbation among bird species, including parrots, is natural, despite prevailing assumptions that it is a harmful behavior in response to environmental factors.

phys-org.title: 'Mini-Neptune' exoplanets may have smoggy atmospheres similar to diesel exhaust
phys-org.description: The astronauts circling Earth on the Artemis mission sent back beautiful clear photos of the continents, clouds, and oceans. But we might be the exception. Many planets in the universe may be hazed in clouds of soot, according to a new study by University of Chicago scientists. Their analysis explains a curious trend seen by astronomers training telescopes on distant planets beyond our own solar system. Many of these worlds had atmospheres that returned strangely featureless readings.

phys-org.title: How a Richard Feynman formula could explain your dining habits in a new city
phys-org.description: One of the dilemmas facing anyone in a new and unfamiliar city is where to dine out. You might consult guides, speak to locals, check reviews, and ultimately, try your luck. But if you're there for a while, at some point you're going to be asking yourself whether to visit new eateries or stick to the ones you've already tried and liked.

phys-org.title: Atacama Desert's extreme aridity initiated 20 million years earlier than previously thought, study finds
phys-org.description: A collaborative study with the University of Cologne, recently published in Nature Communications, provides compelling evidence that the extreme aridity in the hyperarid core of the Atacama Desert began over 40 million years ago—significantly earlier than previously assumed. phys-org.title: Modeling life beneath our feet: A step towards realistic soil ecology at the landscape scale
phys-org.description: As soil health becomes a defining goal of the EU Soil Strategy for 2030, researchers at Aarhus University are rethinking how we model what lives beneath our feet. Their new spatially explicit population model for the soil invertebrate Folsomia candida (springtails) marks a significant step beyond standard laboratory testing.

phys-org.title: The risk of relationship breakdown can be influenced by our genes
phys-org.description: Genetics influences who of us are more likely to experience a relationship breakdown, and who are more likely to remain together. But genes are not decisive, new research shows. "Our destiny does not lie in our genes, but if a relationship were a jigsaw puzzle, our genetics would make up some of the pieces that can influence the risk of a breakup," says sociologist Ruth Eva Jørgensen.

phys-org.title: Britain's oldest cave art may have been rediscovered in Bacon Hole cave
phys-org.description: The oldest cave art in Britain may have been discovered, or more likely rediscovered, in a cave on the Gower Peninsula in South Wales, possibly dating back around 17,000 years.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

undark.title: Medicine’s Move Toward Race-Neutral Risk Assessments
undark.description: Earlier this year, new guidelines were released for doctors assessing a patient’s risk for heart disease. The guidelines take a race-neutral and patient-informed approach that’s rooted in up-to-date science, one doctor writes, and offer a glimpse of a future in which health equity is the standard in medicine.

undark.title: In Coal Country, Black Lung Surges as Federal Protections Stall
undark.description: While the Trump administration is directing hundreds of millions of dollars to coal projects, miners in Appalachia are suffering from a resurgence of black lung disease. But industry pushback is delaying federal rules that would reduce miners’ exposure to deadly silica dust.

proj-syn.title: British Steel Needs a Transformation, Not a Bailout
proj-syn.description: The recent revival of industrial policy offers an opportunity to break the old pattern whereby economic risks are socialized while rewards remain privatized. In addition to attaching meaningful conditionalities to public support, governments must invest in the state capacity required to govern strategic sectors well.

proj-syn.title: How to Encourage Deceased Organ Donation
proj-syn.description: Developing countries facing organ shortages often search for complex solutions, such as sweeping legal reforms. But Tunisia’s experience suggests a much simpler first step: awareness-raising sessions where doctors explain how the transplant system works, and people share their fears and concerns.

proj-syn.title: Building Alliances of America’s Allies
proj-syn.description: In a world in which the US cannot be counted on as it once was, the objective is not stability at any price, but rather stability on terms consistent with national and Western interests. This is achievable, but only if the friends of the US recognize the new reality and act individually and collectively to meet the challenge.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Limits of African Data Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: African countries are recognizing that no matter how well-designed their data-protection regulations are, their sovereignty over US-based Big Tech firms ends at the boundary between subsidiary and parent. Overcoming this barrier will require a level of coordination that the continent has yet to achieve.

proj-syn.title: The AI Economy’s Permanent Underclass
proj-syn.description: AI is transforming the global economy while widening the gap between technological winners and losers. Governments that fail to secure a place in the AI supply chain may find themselves confronting mass job displacement without the tax revenues or state capacity needed to contain the social and political fallout.

proj-syn.title: The Rape of Venezuela
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s oil production is rising, yet its currency is depreciating, inflation is accelerating, and foreign exchange remains scarce. The disconnect reflects a political economy built on private dealmaking and a mutually beneficial alliance between ruling elites and US President Donald Trump’s acolytes.

proj-syn.title: The One Man Who Could Give Trump Middle East Peace
proj-syn.description: With a large majority of UN member states recognizing Palestine on the 1967 lines, there is a clear international blueprint for creating an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. What has been missing is credible Palestinian leadership of the kind that the imprisoned politician Marwan Barghouti could provide.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Nuclear Options
proj-syn.description: The risks raised by nuclear weapons remain as potent as ever, but the institutional framework that mitigated them has been severely eroded. The task now is to prevent deterrence from giving way to proliferation—which, for Europe, means building conventional capabilities, keeping the US engaged, and upholding restraint.

proj-syn.title: The Intelligence That AI Is Missing
proj-syn.description: For AI to simplify humans’ complex social and professional lives, it cannot just give tidy answers based on whatever the internet has to say about our values. It will need the capacity to account for our relational commitments, which are typically grounded in personal identity, experience, and culture.

proj-syn.title: Why Isn’t Europe Poorer Than the US?
proj-syn.description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman has a point when he says that European living standards have largely kept pace with those in the US, despite flagging growth and innovation. But this will not remain true indefinitely: restoring Europe's ability to compete at the technological frontier remains essential to its future well-being.

proj-syn.title: The Real Choice Confronting Developing Countries
proj-syn.description: Lost in the debate about whether developing countries should pursue manufacturing- or services-led growth is the potential for new AI tools to make even informal workers far more productive. If governments can broaden access to such technologies, they no longer need to choose between strategies.

proj-syn.title: India’s Great Political Realignment
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party’s focus on religious identity, together with its “purification” of voter rolls, has created a more binary—and potentially volatile—political landscape, where elections increasingly reflect ethno-religious identity. This month’s elections in five states largely confirmed this trend.

proj-syn.title: Central Banking in an Age of Global Supply Shocks
proj-syn.description: The core assumptions underlying the decades-old inflation-targeting orthodoxy have proven to be unfit for a geopolitically fragmented world characterized by frequent supply-side disruptions. Under such conditions, central banks' traditional monetary policies are only as effective as markets believe them to be.

proj-syn.title: The Tech-MAGA Breakup Is Coming
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has managed to fuse a backward-looking populist movement with a Silicon Valley vanguard whose guiding assumption is that AI will render a large share of ordinary people economically redundant. But with the tech billionaires now rewiring America's electricity grid and driving up costs, a split seems inevitable.

proj-syn.title: A Professor Should Work Hard and Grade Easy
